# Independent audit of exact sector replacement

Source: `candidate be9098c627b40217`, final Sections 1--6.

**PASS; no correction requested.** This is an ordinary planar theorem,
not a mixed-fiber compatibility reduction.

I checked the endpoint-wedge classification, including p=1 or q=1,
negative support coefficients, parallel supports, and the unbounded
D<=0 branch. The positive support combination proves the bounded
quadrilateral description and its exact area. In the unbounded branch
(-p,1) is an actual positive recession direction. Both explicit choices
of V are finite, belong to the wedge, have positive coordinates, and
satisfy u+v=2alpha, including the core-area equality case.

The proposed four-point sector polygon has exactly the required area.
Its max-linear gauge is positive away from zero and agrees with the
radial coordinate on both sector boundaries. Membership of V in the
original wedge gives the two coefficient inequalities needed for this
gauge to dominate both original supporting forms.

The global gluing argument is valid. A line avoiding the origin meets
sector rays transversely whenever it meets them; the two adjacent
convex restrictions agree with a common affine lower support there.
Their one-sided slopes therefore cannot decrease. Lines through zero
are handled separately by positive homogeneity and positivity. This
establishes convexity of the glued function on every line, rather than
assuming that the union of the sector polygons is convex. Local
containment near a prescribed endpoint and global convexity then imply
that each original chosen line supports the entire new polygon.

Every specified ray endpoint and sector area is unchanged. Opposite
endpoints determine the original central chord exactly. The six
oriented cap areas are sums of sector areas; the boundary rays have
zero area. The count is at most one new vertex per open sector plus
the prescribed endpoints, hence at most 12 for three distinct central
lines. Redundant prescribed points only reduce this count.

I reran `supporting computation verify_fixed_endpoint_sector_polygon_replacement_slab_recovery.py`:
32,735 exact checks PASS, with core, bounded and unbounded wedges all
exercised. The general proof does not rely on that finite check.

The source correctly declines Hausdorff closeness, preservation of
unrecorded directions, triangle reduction, and compatibility with
neighboring mixed fibers. New vertices may lie outside the old body;
these limitations are substantive and retained.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
